endpoints.coordinateEvidenceDetail: ia_dnr_story_sopers_mill_access_235_feature_218_20260918 b8930fe9-14ab-4667-b94f-40cc4eb24579: Iowa DNR's public access feature 218 is Sopers Mill A, access number 235, in Story County, managed and owned by the county conservation board, with a 10-by-71-foot concrete access surface, 20 gravel parking stalls, and parking 10 feet from access. Its published South Skunk River coordinate is 42.104244318429394,-93.5729709396775. The same GIS contains nearby feature 1312 (Sopers Mill B) with fewer site identity attributes; this control follows feature 218 and confirms the access point, not a surveyed wet toe.
endpoints.note: Stored coordinate matches the named authoritative access-area control (ia_dnr_story_sopers_mill_access_235_feature_218_20260918 b8930fe9-14ab-4667-b94f-40cc4eb24579) on South Skunk River; this confirms the public access site, not the exact water-edge point. Confirm the water-edge location and carry before paddling.

endpoints.coordinateEvidenceDetail: ia_story_lekwa_ramp_water_entry a39ce3e3-b29c-4f3b-8334-4f19ff04c40c: Story County identifies Lekwa Access #242 at 56156 130th Street as a managed South Skunk River Water Trail access, and the official MyCountyParks record independently documents canoeing and kayaking with photographs of the signed access and its ramp reaching the river. The matching Iowa DNR public water-access inventory feature (GlobalID a39ce3e3-b29c-4f3b-8334-4f19ff04c40c) describes a concrete launch with six parking stalls and a 33-foot parking-to-access distance. Current Esri World Imagery places that inventory coordinate at the visible water-side ramp edge immediately south of the 130th Street bridge. It is retained as the water entry; the NHD and route-projected alternatives 23 and 50 feet farther east are rejected because they move into the channel.
endpoints.note: Stored coordinate matches the exact named authoritative water-entry control (ia_story_lekwa_ramp_water_entry a39ce3e3-b29c-4f3b-8334-4f19ff04c40c) on South Skunk River; the 50 ft named-flowline offset reflects incomplete or generalized NHD coverage, not a proposed coordinate move.
